samples.summary: docs-view's new `readOnly` effect dependency and `store.dispose()` cleanup have no test, while the identical change in notes and slides each got one
samples.evidence: The diff adds `readOnly` to the effect deps and a `store.dispose()` call in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx`, and ships new remount tests only for notes (`notes-view-readonly.test.tsx`) and slides (`slides-view-readonly.test.tsx`). No docs-view test exists: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/**/*.test.*` contains only `image-insert.test.ts`, and `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/*` has no docs-view file. If the deps line regresses, an editor→viewer downgrade on /shared/:token leaves a fully writable docs editor over a document the session may no longer write — exactly the failure the notes/slides tests were added to prevent — and nothing catches it.

samples.summary: `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` (unsubscribe + clear onRemoteChange) is new and has no test
samples.evidence: `dispose()` is added to YorkieDocStore and called from docs-view's cleanup, but `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` contains no occurrence of `dispose(` or `onRemoteChange` (grep returned no matches), and the only `.dispose()` calls under packages/frontend/tests are in pdf-collab.test.tsx for a different store. A regression (subscription not released, or an already-queued callback still firing) would let a discarded store keep driving a disposed editor on every remote change — the leak this method exists to close — with no failing test.

samples.summary: The revalidation/eviction logic in SharedDocumentByToken is only covered at the pure-predicate level; the component decision `fatal = error && (!resolved || isRevoked)` is untested
samples.evidence: `share-links.test.ts` tests `isRevokedShareLinkError` in isolation, which is good, but the behaviour the change is about — a background refetch failure must NOT tear down a live session while `resolved` is retained, a verdict MUST close the view, and the token is re-resolved on `SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` — lives in the new `useQuery` wiring in shared-document.tsx. No test renders SharedDocumentByToken: grep for `SharedDocumentByToken`/`useQuery`/`resolveShareLink` across frontend tests matches only share-links.test.ts and unrelated files. If the composition inverted, a laptop-sleep blip would evict a live editing session and lose unsynced edits.

samples.summary: `requestLayoutRefresh`'s dirty-set save/restore (the anti-full-remeasure seam) has no test
samples.evidence: editor.ts now wires `textEditor.requestLayoutRefresh = () => { const dirty = dirtyBlockIds; recomputeLayout(); dirtyBlockIds = dirty ?? new Set(); }` with a long comment claiming (a) the deferred paint stays incremental and (b) `getLayout()` is fresh mid-unit so the paste path's `blockParentMap` branch is correct. Grep across packages/docs/test finds `requestLayoutRefresh` only in editor-read-only.test.ts's unrelated matches and no test asserting either property; `incremental-layout.test.ts` is untouched. The frontend paint-count test only counts paints, not measures. A regression here silently re-measures the whole document on every batched keystroke (perf) or branches on a stale layout during paste.

samples.summary: `revocableDocStore`'s proxy traps and memoization are only covered for the write/read case; the revoked-state traps and the live-identity claim are untested
samples.evidence: The new `revocableDocStore` implements `set`, `defineProperty`, `deleteProperty`, `getPrototypeOf` (null when revoked), `setPrototypeOf`, `preventExtensions`, `isExtensible`, `has`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` and `ownKeys`, plus a memoized bound-member cache whose documented purpose is identity stability (`s.canUndo === s.canUndo`). The new 'a disposed editor is inert' block in packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts only exercises mutator no-ops and reads; the existing trap tests (e.g. line 843 preventExtensions, line 852 `in`) run against the read-only mount, which never goes through this proxy. So a wrong trap (e.g. `ownKeys` exposing internals, or `Object.freeze` on the live handle breaking the invariant) would ship green.

samples.summary: The new `isDisposed()` guard in `insertImageFromUrl` has no test; only the file path got one
samples.evidence: image-insert.test.ts adds 'inserts nothing when the editor was disposed under the upload' for `insertImageFromFile` only. There is no describe block for `insertImageFromUrl` in the file at all, so its identical post-await guard (and the `return false` it returns) is uncovered — a stale write into a document the session may no longer edit would go undetected.

samples.summary: The table-cell-range branch of the new style batching (both editor.ts and text-editor.ts) has no undo-unit test
samples.evidence: Both `applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts, `doc.batch(() => applyStyleToCellRange(cellRange, style))`) and `TextEditor.applyStyleToSelection` (text-editor.ts, `withUndoUnit(() => this.doc.applyInlineStyleToCells(...))`) were changed for #1045, but every new undo-unit test in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts uses paragraph ranges. Grep for `applyStyleToCellRange` / `applyInlineStyleToCells` across packages/docs/test yields only a comment in editor-read-only.test.ts. A cell range wider than Yorkie's 50-entry cap would lose styling undo exactly as the paragraph case did, with no test to notice.

samples.summary: The two new Cmd+Shift+V guard tests are negative-only with no proof the paste path was ever entered — they would pass vacuously if the shortcut never fired
samples.evidence: Both new tests dispatch `dispatchPastePlain(textarea)` and then assert the clipboard payload is absent ('PLAIN' not in text / text === 'seed'). Nothing asserts that `readText()` was actually called or that the handler was reached (`installPendingClipboard` returns no spy), and there is no positive control in this file showing the same dispatch DOES paste when alive. If the keydown routing changed (e.g. the mod/shift gate at text-editor.ts:1373) both tests would still pass while the `disposed`/`pasting` guards went unexercised.
searchedFor: read the new tests in the diff

samples.summary: 'insertText over a multi-block selection is one undo unit' cannot distinguish a working Cmd+A from a failed one
samples.evidence: If the synthetic Cmd/Ctrl+A never selected anything, `insertText('X')` would still open exactly one outermost batch and `writesOutsideABatch()` would still be 0, and the follow-up `undo()` would still restore ['alpha','beta'] — so every assertion in the test holds whether or not the multi-block selection existed. The sibling test ('insertText really writes what it was given', asserting ['X']) is what actually proves the selection, but it uses a separate mount and does not run the batch watcher.
searchedFor: read the new text-box-editor tests in the diff

samples.summary: `withUndoUnit`'s documented 'replayed once, including after a throw' render behaviour is untested for the throwing case
samples.evidence: The doc comment on `withUndoUnit` claims held renders are replayed at most once after the outermost unit commits 'including after a throw'. The only paint-count coverage is the frontend test 'paints once for the whole action, after the unit commits', which uses a non-throwing body. No test drives a body that throws, so a leaked `renderAfterUndoUnit` flag or a permanently stuck `undoUnitDepth` after an exception would not be caught.

finding.evidence: The diff adds `readOnly` to the effect deps and a `store.dispose()` call in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx`, and ships new remount tests only for notes (`notes-view-readonly.test.tsx`) and slides (`slides-view-readonly.test.tsx`). No docs-view test exists: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/**/*.test.*` contains only `image-insert.test.ts`, and `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/*` has no docs-view file. If the deps line regresses, an editor→viewer downgrade on /shared/:token leaves a fully writable docs editor over a document the session may no longer write — exactly the failure the notes/slides tests were added to prevent — and nothing catches it.

verdict.reason: docs-view.tsx really does carry the readOnly-keyed rebuild (deps `[didMount, doc, readOnly]` at line 590) and the new `store.dispose()` cleanup (line 574), and no test anywhere exercises it. I searched well beyond the reviewer's queries: repo-wide glob for *readonly* test files (only notes-view-readonly.test.tsx and slides-view-readonly.test.tsx), grep for `DocsView` across all *.test/*.spec files (only two comment mentions in docs-context-menu/docs-table-context-menu tests), grep for `rerender(` across packages/frontend (12 files, only the notes/slides readonly tests do a readOnly flip), full listing of packages/frontend/tests/**/*docs* and packages/frontend/**/*.test.tsx, plus indirect routes: packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts covers a disposed editor's inertness inside the editor package (not that the host re-runs the effect or calls store.dispose()), image-insert.test.ts only mentions the downgrade in a comment, tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts contains no `dispose` at all, and src/app/shared/__tests__ has only blob routing. There are no frontend .spec/e2e view tests. The notes/slides tests show exactly what the docs equivalent would look like (assert initialize re-called with true and dispose called once), so the asymmetry is real. Impact matches major: a regression to the deps line leaves a fully writable docs editor for a /shared/:token session downgraded editor→viewer, and nothing would catch it.
